name: Temporal Coherence Map
description: Maps temporal coherence across frames. This method precisely identifies AI-generated content through deep statistical analysis.
algorithm: Temporal Coherence Map — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method creates temporal coherence maps for deepfake detection:

1. **Feature Tracking Across Frames**: Dense feature correspondences are established between consecutive frames using optical flow, and long-range correspondences across multiple frames using feature matching. This creates a spatio-temporal feature trajectory map.

2. **Local Coherence Computation**: For each pixel, temporal coherence is computed as the consistency of its feature trajectory — smooth, physically plausible trajectories have high coherence, while erratic or discontinuous trajectories have low coherence. The coherence map reveals regions with temporal instability.

3. **Coherence Map Spatial Analysis**: Natural video shows uniformly high coherence for static regions and physically motivated coherence patterns for moving objects. The method analyzes the coherence map for anomalous low-coherence regions — deepfake-generated areas often show reduced temporal coherence, particularly at face boundaries and in texture regions.

4. **Face-Background Coherence Comparison**: The average coherence in face regions vs. background provides a diagnostic ratio. In authentic video, both show similar coherence levels. Deepfakes typically show lower coherence in the generated face (per-frame independent generation) compared to the naturally captured background.

5. **Coherence Temporal Trends**: The per-frame average coherence is tracked over time. Natural video maintains high, stable coherence. Deepfake videos may show coherence drops correlated with challenging face poses, expressions, or lighting conditions where the generator produces more temporally inconsistent output.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through temporal coherence map analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Zheng, Y. et al. (2021). Exploring Temporal Coherence for More General Video Face Forgery Detection. ICCV.
Amerini, I. et al. (2019). Deepfake Video Detection through Optical Flow based CNN. ICCV Workshop.
